title.zh: 第十八 五行六 日蝕 日抱 日赤無光 日黃珥 日中黑 虹貫日 月蝕非其月
title.raw: 第十八 五行六 日蝕 日抱 日赤無光 日黃珥 日中黑 虹貫日 月蝕非其月 Volume 108: Five Elements Part Six

sentences.zh: 志第十八 五行六

translations.literal: Treatise Eighteen: The Five Phases, Part Six.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 18: The Five Phases, Part Six.

sentences.zh: 日蚀 日抱 日赤无光 日黄珥 日中黑 虹贯日 月蚀非其月

translations.literal: Solar eclipses; the sun embraced; the sun red yet without light; the sun with yellow ear-rings; black within the sun; a rainbow piercing the sun; lunar eclipse not in its proper month.
translations.idiomatic: Solar eclipse; the haloed sun; the sun dimmed to a dull red; yellow prominences on the solar disk; a dark spot on the face of the sun; a rainbow across the sun; a lunar eclipse out of season.

sentences.zh: 光武帝建武二年正月甲子朔，日有蚀之，在危八度。

translations.literal: On the jiazi new-moon day of the first month in the second year of Jianwu of Emperor Guangwu, there was a solar eclipse, at eight degrees in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon, jiazi, in the first month of Jianwu 2 (26 CE), a solar eclipse occurred at eight degrees within the lodge Wei.

sentences.zh: 《日蚀说》曰：「日者，太阳之精，人君之象。

translations.literal: The Treatise on Solar Eclipses says: "The sun is the essence of great yang, the image of the human ruler."
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on Solar Eclipses reads: "The sun embodies supreme yang; it is the emblem of the sovereign."

sentences.zh: 君道有亏，有阴所乘，故蚀。

translations.literal: The ruler's way having defect, yin rides upon it; therefore it eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler's conduct falls short, yin force overtakes the sun, and an eclipse follows.

sentences.zh: 蚀者，阳不克也。

translations.literal: Eclipse means yang does not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: An eclipse means yang has lost its ascendancy.

sentences.zh: 」其候杂说，《汉书·五行志》著之必矣。

translations.literal: As for the various predictive glosses, the Treatise on the Five Phases in the Han shu records them in full.
translations.idiomatic: The assorted prognostic glosses are set out at length in the Han shu Treatise on the Five Phases.

sentences.zh: 儒说诸侯专权，则其应多在日所宿之国。

translations.literal: Confucian explanation: when feudal lords monopolize power, then its responses are mostly in the state where the sun lodges.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars hold that when regional lords seize unchecked power, the omen usually falls on the state whose celestial lodge the sun occupies.

sentences.zh: 诸象附从，则多为王者事。

translations.literal: When various images attach and follow, then mostly they are matters of the king.
translations.idiomatic: When secondary portents cluster with the eclipse, they tend to concern the throne itself.

sentences.zh: 人君改修其德，则咎害除。

translations.literal: If the human ruler reforms and cultivates his virtue, then blame and harm are removed.
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler mends his ways and cultivates virtue, the ill omen and its harm may be dispelled.

sentences.zh: 是时，世祖初兴，天下贼乱未除。

translations.literal: At this time the Shizu had first risen, and bandit turmoil under Heaven was not yet removed.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu had only just restored the dynasty; rebels still roamed the empire.

sentences.zh: 虚、危，齐也。

translations.literal: Xu and Wei are Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The lodges Xu and Wei correspond to the old territory of Qi.

sentences.zh: 贼张步拥兵据齐，上遣伏隆谕步，许降。

translations.literal: The bandit Zhang Bu held troops and occupied Qi; the sovereign sent Fu Long to instruct Bu, promising acceptance of surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The warlord Zhang Bu held Qi with an army; the emperor sent Fu Long to negotiate and accepted his offer to submit.

sentences.zh: 旋复叛称王，至五年中乃破。

translations.literal: Soon he again rebelled and declared himself king; down to the middle of the fifth year he was then broken.
translations.idiomatic: He soon rebelled again, proclaimed himself king, and was not crushed until mid–Jianwu 5.

sentences.zh: 三年五月乙卯晦，日有蚀之，在柳十四度。

translations.literal: On the last day yimao of the fifth month of the third year, there was a solar eclipse, at fourteen degrees in Liu.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on yimao in the fifth month of Jianwu 3 (27), the sun was eclipsed at fourteen degrees in Liu.

sentences.zh: 柳，河南也。

translations.literal: Liu is Henan south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Liu maps to the Henan region south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 时，世祖在雒阳，赤眉降贼樊崇谋作乱，其七月发觉，皆伏诛。

translations.literal: At the time the Shizu was in Luoyang; the surrendered Red Eyebrow bandit Fan Chong plotted rebellion; in the seventh month it was discovered, and all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was at Luoyang when Fan Chong of the surrendered Red Eyebrows plotted a coup; the plot surfaced in the seventh month and the conspirators were put to death.

sentences.zh: 六年九月丙寅晦，日有蚀之。

translations.literal: On the last day bingyin of the ninth month of the sixth year, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on bingyin in the ninth month of Jianwu 6 (30), a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 史官不见，郡以闻。

translations.literal: The clerks of history did not see it; a commandery reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Court astronomers missed it; word came in from a commandery.

sentences.zh: 在尾八度。

translations.literal: It was at eight degrees in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The sun stood at eight degrees in Wei.

sentences.zh: 七年三月癸亥晦，日有蚀之，在毕五度。

translations.literal: On the last day guihai of the third month of the seventh year, there was a solar eclipse, at five degrees in Bi.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on guihai in the third month of Jianwu 7 (31), an eclipse fell at five degrees in Bi.

sentences.zh: 毕为边兵。

translations.literal: Bi is border troops.
translations.idiomatic: Bi presages warfare on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 秋，隗嚣反，侵安定。

translations.literal: In autumn Wei Xiao rebelled and invaded Anding.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Wei Xiao rose in revolt and struck into Anding.

sentences.zh: 冬，卢芳所置朔方、云中太守各举郡降。

translations.literal: In winter the Shuofang and Yunzhong governors installed by Lu Fang each raised their commanderies and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In winter the puppet governors of Shuofang and Yunzhong whom Lu Fang had appointed surrendered their commands.

sentences.zh: 十六年三月辛丑晦，日有独之，在昴七度。

translations.literal: On the last day xinchou of the third month of the sixteenth year, there was a solar eclipse, at seven degrees in Mao.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on xinchou in the third month of Jianwu 16 (40), the sun was eclipsed at seven degrees in Mao.

sentences.zh: 昂为狱事。

translations.literal: Mao is prison affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Mao governs prisons and penal cases.

sentences.zh: 时诸郡太守坐度田不实，世祖怒，杀十余人，然后深悔之。

translations.literal: At the time various commandery governors sat guilty of untrue land measurement; the Shizu was angry and killed more than ten persons, afterward deeply regretting it.
translations.idiomatic: Several commandery governors had falsified their land surveys; Guangwu flew into a rage and executed more than a dozen, then bitterly repented.

sentences.zh: 十七年二月乙未晦，日有蚀之，在胃九度。

translations.literal: On the last day yiwei of the second month of the seventeenth year, there was a solar eclipse, at nine degrees in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on yiwei in the second month of Jianwu 17 (41), an eclipse occurred at nine degrees in Wei.

sentences.zh: 胃为廪仓。

translations.literal: Wei is the granary.
translations.idiomatic: Wei signifies the state granaries.

sentences.zh: 时诸郡新坐租之后，天下忧怖，以谷为言，故示象。

translations.literal: At the time the various commanderies had newly suffered punishment over rent; all under Heaven was anxious and fearful, speaking in terms of grain; therefore it showed an image.
translations.idiomatic: Commanderies had just been fined for tax irregularities; the realm was anxious and talk ran to grain shortages—hence Heaven mirrored the distress in the sky.

sentences.zh: 或曰：胃，供养之官也。

translations.literal: Some say: Wei is the office of provision and support.
translations.idiomatic: Others read Wei as the palace department that supplies the court.

sentences.zh: 其十月，废郭皇后，诏曰「不可以奉供养」。

translations.literal: In that tenth month Empress Guo was deposed; an edict said "she cannot undertake provision and support."
translations.idiomatic: That October Empress Guo was cast aside with an edict declaring her unfit to "maintain the ancestral sacrifices."

sentences.zh: 二十二年五月乙未晦，日有蚀之，在柳七度，京都宿也。

translations.literal: On the last day yiwei of the fifth month of the twenty-second year, there was a solar eclipse, at seven degrees in Liu, the capital's lodging.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on yiwei in the fifth month of Jianwu 22 (46), the sun was eclipsed at seven degrees in Liu—the lodge of the capital itself.

sentences.zh: 柳为上仓，祭祀谷也，近舆鬼，舆鬼为宗庙。

translations.literal: Liu is the upper granary, grain for sacrifice; it is near Yugi; Yugi is the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Liu is the "upper granary" of ritual grain; it neighbors Yugi, the asterism of the ancestral shrine.

sentences.zh: 十九年中，有司奏请立近帝四庙以祭之，有诏「庙处所未定，且就高庙袷祭之。

translations.literal: In the midst of the nineteenth year, responsible officials memorialized requesting to establish four temples to recent emperors to sacrifice to them; there was an edict: "The site of the temples is not yet fixed; for now perform the xia sacrifice at the High Temple."
translations.idiomatic: Midway through Jianwu 19, officials asked to dedicate four shrines to the recent emperors; the throne replied that sites were still undecided and ordered joint rites at Gaozu's temple for the time being.

sentences.zh: 」至此三年，遂不立庙。

translations.literal: From then three years passed, and temples were still not established.
translations.idiomatic: Three years passed, and still no separate shrines were built.

sentences.zh: 有简堕心，奉祖宗之道有阙，故示象也。

translations.literal: There was neglect and slackness of mind; the way of honoring the ancestors had gaps; therefore it showed an image.
translations.idiomatic: The court had grown slack toward the ancestors; the rites owed to the imperial dead were neglected—hence the warning in the heavens.

sentences.zh: 二十五年三月戊申晦，日有蚀之，在毕十五度。

translations.literal: On the last day wushen of the third month of the twenty-fifth year, there was a solar eclipse, at fifteen degrees in Bi.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on wushen in the third month of Jianwu 25 (49), an eclipse fell at fifteen degrees in Bi.

sentences.zh: 毕为边兵。

translations.literal: Bi is border troops.
translations.idiomatic: Again Bi pointed to frontier war.

sentences.zh: 其冬十月，以武谿蛮夷为寇害，伏波将军马援将兵击之。

translations.literal: That winter in the tenth month, because the Wuxi Man and Yi were raiding harm, General Who Crosses the Waves Ma Yuan led troops to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month, Ma Yuan marched south against the Wuxi tribes who were plundering the border.

sentences.zh: 二十九年二月丁巳朔，日有蚀之，在东壁五度。

translations.literal: On the dingsi new-moon day of the second month of the twenty-ninth year, there was a solar eclipse, at five degrees in Eastern Wall.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon dingsi in the second month of Jianwu 29 (53), the sun was eclipsed at five degrees in Eastern Wall.

sentences.zh: 东壁为文章，一名娵訾之口。

translations.literal: Eastern Wall is literary composition; one name is the mouth of Ju zi.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wall governs letters and learning; it is also called the mouth of the Ju zi lunar mansion.

sentences.zh: 先是皇子诸王各招来文章谈说之士，去年中，有人上奏：「诸王所招待者，或真伪杂，受刑罚者子孙，宜可分别。

translations.literal: Earlier the imperial sons and various kings each summoned men of letters and disputers; in the previous year someone memorialized: "Those whom the kings entertain are sometimes mixed true and false; descendants of those who suffered punishment should be distinguished."
translations.idiomatic: The princes had been patronizing scholars and debaters; the year before, a memorial warned that their clients included descendants of convicted men and demanded a vetting process.

sentences.zh: 」于是上怒，诏捕诸王客，皆被以苛法，死者甚多。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the sovereign was angry, edicting to arrest the kings' guests; all were charged under harsh law, and the dead were very many.
translations.idiomatic: " Enraged, Guangwu ordered a sweep of the princes' retainers; harsh statutes were applied and many died."

sentences.zh: 世祖不早为明设刑禁，一时治之过差，故天示象。

translations.literal: The Shizu had not early set clear penal prohibitions; in one moment governance overshot; therefore Heaven showed an image.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had not laid down clear rules in advance, the purge overshot its mark—so Heaven sent a sign.

sentences.zh: 世祖于是改悔，遣使悉理侵枉也。

translations.literal: The Shizu thereupon repented and sent envoys to fully rectify encroachments and wrongs.
translations.idiomatic: He then relented and dispatched agents to redress every wrongful conviction.

sentences.zh: 三十一年五月癸酉晦，日有蚀之，在柳五度，京都宿也。

translations.literal: On the last day guiyou of the fifth month of the thirty-first year, there was a solar eclipse, at five degrees in Liu, the capital's lodging.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on guiyou in the fifth month of Jianwu 31 (55), an eclipse struck Liu at five degrees—the capital's own lodge.

sentences.zh: 自二十一年示象至此十年，后二年，宫车晏驾。

translations.literal: From the twenty-first year's showing of image down to here ten years; after two years, the palace carriage delayed its departure (the emperor died).
translations.idiomatic: Ten years had passed since the omen of Jianwu 21; two years after this eclipse, Guangwu died.

sentences.zh: 中元元年十一月甲子晦，日有蚀之，在斗二十度。

translations.literal: On the last day jiazi of the eleventh month of the first year of Zhongyuan, there was a solar eclipse, at twenty degrees in Dou.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on jiazi in the eleventh month of Zhongyuan 1 (56), the sun was eclipsed at twenty degrees in Dou.

sentences.zh: 斗为庙，主爵禄。

translations.literal: Dou is the temple; it governs enfeoffment and salary.
translations.idiomatic: Dou is the lodge of the ancestral shrine and of titles and stipends.

sentences.zh: 儒说十一月甲子，时王日也，又为星纪，主爵禄，其占重。

translations.literal: Confucian explanation: eleventh month jiazi is the king day of the hour; it is also Star Marker; it governs enfeoffment and salary; its prognostication is weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars note that jiazi in the eleventh month is the "king" stem-branch day, and the month belongs to the Star Marker cycle—both tie to rank and revenue, so the omen weighed heavily.

sentences.zh: 明帝永平三年八月壬申晦，日有蚀之，在氐二度。

translations.literal: On the last day renshen of the eighth month of the third year of Yongping of Emperor Ming, there was a solar eclipse, at two degrees in Di.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on renshen in the eighth month of Yongping 3 (60), an eclipse occurred at two degrees in Di.

sentences.zh: 氐为宿宫。

translations.literal: Di is the lodging palace.
translations.idiomatic: Di is the lodge of the ruler's sleeping quarters.

sentences.zh: 是时明帝作北宫。

translations.literal: At this time Emperor Ming was building the Northern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming was then raising the Northern Palace.

sentences.zh: 八年十月壬寅晦，日有蚀之，既，在斗十一度。

translations.literal: On the last day renyin of the eighth month of the eighth year, there was a solar eclipse; it was total, at eleven degrees in Dou.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on renyin in the eighth month of Yongping 8 (65), a total eclipse reached eleven degrees in Dou.

sentences.zh: 斗，吴也。

translations.literal: Dou is Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Dou corresponds to the old state of Wu.

sentences.zh: 广陵于天文属吴。

translations.literal: Guangling in astronomical terms belongs to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: By celestial reckoning Guangling lies in the Wu sector.

sentences.zh: 后二年，广陵王荆坐谋反自杀。

translations.literal: After two years Prince Jing of Guangling sat guilty of plotting rebellion and committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Prince Jing of Guangling killed himself after a conviction for treason.

sentences.zh: 十三年十月甲辰晦，日有蚀之，在尾十七度。

translations.literal: On the last day jiachen of the tenth month of the thirteenth year, there was a solar eclipse, at seventeen degrees in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on jiachen in the tenth month of Yongping 13 (70), the sun was eclipsed at seventeen degrees in Wei.

sentences.zh: 十六年五月戊午晦，日有蚀之，在柳十五度。

translations.literal: On the last day wuwu of the fifth month of the sixteenth year, there was a solar eclipse, at fifteen degrees in Liu.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on wuwu in the fifth month of Yongping 16 (73), an eclipse fell at fifteen degrees in Liu.

sentences.zh: 儒说五月戊午，犹十一月甲子也，又宿在京都，其占重。

translations.literal: Confucian explanation: fifth month wuwu is like eleventh month jiazi; moreover the lodging is at the capital region; its prognostication is weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars liken wuwu in the fifth month to jiazi in the eleventh month, and Liu again marked the capital—so the portent was grave.

sentences.zh: 后二岁，宫车晏驾。

translations.literal: After two years the palace carriage delayed its departure.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Emperor Ming died.

sentences.zh: 十八年十一月甲辰晦，日有蚀之，在斗二十一度。

translations.literal: On the last day jiachen of the eleventh month of the eighteenth year, there was a solar eclipse, at twenty-one degrees in Dou.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on jiachen in the eleventh month of Yongping 18 (75), an eclipse occurred at twenty-one degrees in Dou.

sentences.zh: 是时，明帝既崩，马太后制爵禄，故阳不胜。

translations.literal: At this time Emperor Ming had already died; Empress Dowager Ma controlled enfeoffment and salary; therefore yang did not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Ming had just died, and Empress Dowager Ma held the power of appointments—yang, the masculine principle of rule, was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 章帝建初五年二月庚辰朔，日有蚀之，在东壁八度。

translations.literal: On the gengchen new-moon day of the second month of the fifth year of Jianchu of Emperor Zhang, there was a solar eclipse, at eight degrees in Eastern Wall.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon gengchen in the second month of Zhangdi's Jianchu 5 (80), the sun was eclipsed at eight degrees in Eastern Wall.

sentences.zh: 例在前建武二十九年。

translations.literal: The precedent is before, in Jianwu twenty-ninth year.
translations.idiomatic: The parallel case is recorded under Jianwu 29.

sentences.zh: 是时，群臣争经，多相非毁者。

translations.literal: At this time the various ministers disputed the classics, many mutually slandering.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers were wrangling over exegetical tradition and tearing one another down in debate.

sentences.zh: 六年六月辛未晦，日有蚀之，在翼六度。

translations.literal: On the last day xinwei of the sixth month of the sixth year, there was a solar eclipse, at six degrees in Yi.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on xinwei in the sixth month of Jianchu 6 (81), an eclipse struck six degrees in Yi.

sentences.zh: 翼主远客。

translations.literal: Yi governs distant guests.
translations.idiomatic: Yi presages envoys and guests from afar.

sentences.zh: 冬，东平王苍等来朝，明年正月，苍薨。

translations.literal: In winter Prince Cang of Dongping and others came to court; in the first month of the next year Cang died.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Prince Cang of Dongping attended court; he died the following first month.

sentences.zh: 章和元年八月乙未晦，日有蚀之。

translations.literal: On the last day yiwei of the eighth month of the first year of Zhanghe, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on yiwei in the eighth month of Zhanghe 1 (87), a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 史官不见，佗官以闻。

translations.literal: The clerks of history did not see it; another official reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Court astronomers missed it; another office relayed the news.

sentences.zh: 日在氐四度。

translations.literal: The sun was at four degrees in Di.
translations.idiomatic: The disk stood at four degrees in Di.

sentences.zh: 和帝永元二年二月壬午，日有蚀之。

translations.literal: On renwu day of the second month of the second year of Yongyuan of Emperor He, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu in the second month of Yongyuan 2 (90), the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 史官不见，涿郡以闻。

translations.literal: The clerks of history did not see it; Zhuo Commandery reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Astronomers at the capital failed to record it; Zhuo Commandery sent word.

sentences.zh: 日在奎八度。

translations.literal: The sun was at eight degrees in Kui.
translations.idiomatic: The eclipse point lay at eight degrees in Kui.

sentences.zh: 四年六月戊戌朔，日有蚀之，在七星二度，主衣裳。

translations.literal: On the wuxu new-moon day of the sixth month of the fourth year, there was a solar eclipse, at two degrees in the Seven Stars; it governs robes and skirts.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon wuxu in the sixth month of Yongyuan 4 (92), the sun was eclipsed at two degrees in the Seven Stars—the lodge of court dress.

sentences.zh: 又曰行近轩辕，在左角，为太后族。

translations.literal: It is also said the course drew near Xuanyuan, at the left horn, being the empress dowager's clan.
translations.idiomatic: Some add that the path brushed Xuanyuan at the left horn—the sector of the empress dowager's kin.

sentences.zh: 是月十九日，上免太后兄弟窦宪等官，遣就国，选严能相，于国蹙迫自杀。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth day of that month the sovereign dismissed the empress dowager's brothers Dou Xian and others from office, sent them to their states, selected stern capable chancellors, and in the states they were pressed and committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth of that month the emperor stripped Dou Xian and his brothers of office, packed them off to their fiefs, installed harsh overseers, and drove them to suicide.

sentences.zh: 七年四月辛亥朔，日有蚀之，在嘴觿，为葆旅，主收敛。

translations.literal: On the xinhai new-moon day of the fourth month of the seventh year, there was a solar eclipse, at Zui and Xi; it is Baolü; it governs gathering in.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon xinhai in the fourth month of Yongyuan 7 (95), an eclipse fell in the Beak asterisms (Zuixi); the lodge signifies mustering hosts and tightening control.

sentences.zh: 儒说葆旅宫中之象，收敛贪妒之象。

translations.literal: Confucian explanation: Baolü is an image inside the palace; gathering in is an image of greed and jealousy.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars read Baolü as a sign of intrigue within the harem—jealous grasping and the reining in of rivals.

sentences.zh: 是岁邓贵人始人。

translations.literal: That year Honored Person Deng first entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: That year Lady Deng entered the palace as a concubine.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，阴皇后立，邓贵人有宠，阴后妒忌之，后遂坐废。

translations.literal: In the third month of the next year Empress Yin was established; Honored Person Deng had favor; Empress Yin was jealous of her; afterward she sat deposed.
translations.idiomatic: The next third month Empress Yin was enthroned while Lady Deng won the emperor's favor; Yin's jealousy led to her own deposition.

sentences.zh: 一曰是将入参，参、伐为斩刈。

translations.literal: One account says it was about to enter Shen; Shen and Fa are execution and cutting.
translations.idiomatic: Another line of interpretation: the sun was moving toward Shen; Shen and the Fa asterism mean beheading and slaughter.

sentences.zh: 明年七月，越骑校尉冯柱捕斩匈奴温禺犊王乌居战。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the next year Colonel of Agile Cavalry Feng Zhu captured and beheaded the Xiongnu King Wenyudou Wuju zhan.
translations.idiomatic: The following seventh month Feng Zhu, colonel of agile cavalry, captured and executed the Xiongnu chieftain Wuju zhan of the Wenyudou royal house.

sentences.zh: 十二年秋七月辛亥朔，日有蚀之，在翼八度，荆州宿也。

translations.literal: On the xinhai new-moon day of the seventh month in autumn of the twelfth year, there was a solar eclipse, at eight degrees in Yi, Jingzhou's lodging.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon xinhai in the seventh month of Yongyuan 12 (100), an eclipse occurred at eight degrees in Yi—the lodge of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，南郡蛮夷反，为寇。

translations.literal: The next winter the Man and Yi of Nan Commandery rebelled and became raiders.
translations.idiomatic: The next winter the southern tribes of Nan Commandery rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 十五年四月甲子晦，日有蚀之，在东井二十二度。

translations.literal: On the last day jiazi of the fourth month of the fifteenth year, there was a solar eclipse, at twenty-two degrees in Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on jiazi in the fourth month of Yongyuan 15 (103), the sun was eclipsed at twenty-two degrees in Eastern Well.

sentences.zh: 东井，主酒食之宿也。

translations.literal: Eastern Well is the lodging that governs wine and food.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Well governs drink and viands—the kitchen of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 妇人之职，无非无仪，酒食是议。

translations.literal: The woman's duty: without fault, without display; wine and food are what she deliberates.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say a woman's sphere is blameless modesty and the ordering of drink and food.

sentences.zh: 去年冬，邓皇后立，有丈夫之性，与知外事，故天示象。

translations.literal: Last winter Empress Deng was established; she had the nature of a man and participated in knowing outer affairs; therefore Heaven showed an image.
translations.idiomatic: The previous winter Empress Deng had been installed; she took a hand in statecraft like a man—Heaven therefore mirrored her overreach in the eclipse.

sentences.zh: 是年水，雨伤稼。

translations.literal: That year there was flood; rain harmed the crops.
translations.idiomatic: The same year floods and relentless rains ruined the harvest.

sentences.zh: 安帝永初元年三月二日癸酉，日有蚀之，在胃二度。

translations.literal: On the second day of the third month guiyou of the first year of Yongchu of Emperor An, there was a solar eclipse, at two degrees in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, the second day of the third month of Yongchu 1 (107), the sun was eclipsed at two degrees in Wei.

sentences.zh: 胃主禀仓。

translations.literal: Wei governs the granary.
translations.idiomatic: Wei again signals the imperial granaries.

sentences.zh: 是时，邓太后专政，去年大水伤稼，仓禀为虚。

translations.literal: At this time Empress Dowager Deng monopolized government; last year great water harmed crops; granaries were empty.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Deng held the reins; the previous year's floods had emptied the bins.

sentences.zh: 五年正月庚辰朔，日有蚀之，在虚八度。

translations.literal: On the gengchen new-moon day of the first month of the fifth year, there was a solar eclipse, at eight degrees in Xu.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon gengchen in the first month of Yongchu 5 (111), an eclipse fell at eight degrees in Xu.

sentences.zh: 正月，王者统事之正日也。

translations.literal: The first month is the correct day when the king presides over affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The first month is the month in which the Son of Heaven sets the year in motion.

sentences.zh: 虚，空名也。

translations.literal: Xu is empty name.
translations.idiomatic: Xu means "void" and "empty title."

sentences.zh: 是时邓太后摄政，安帝不得行事，俱不得其正，若王者位虚，故于正月阳不克，示象也。

translations.literal: At this time Empress Dowager Deng held the regency; Emperor An could not carry out affairs; both did not obtain their correctness; as if the king's position were empty; therefore in the first month yang did not overcome—it showed an image.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager ruled in place of the young emperor, so neither occupied the rightful role—like a vacant throne—hence yang failed on the year's first new moon.

sentences.zh: 于是阴预乘阳，故夷狄并为寇害，西边诸郡皆至虚空。

translations.literal: Thereupon yin beforehand rode yang; therefore the Yi and Di together became raiding harm; the various western commanderies all reached emptiness and void.
translations.idiomatic: Yin thus mounted yang; barbarians raided along every frontier, and the western commanderies were laid waste.

sentences.zh: 七年四月丙申晦，日有蚀之，在东井一度。

translations.literal: On the last day bingshen of the fourth month of the seventh year, there was a solar eclipse, at one degree in Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on bingshen in the fourth month of Yongchu 7 (113), the sun was eclipsed at one degree in Eastern Well.

sentences.zh: 元初元年十月戊子朔，日有蚀之，在尾十度。

translations.literal: On the wuzi new-moon day of the tenth month of the first year of Yuanchu, there was a solar eclipse, at ten degrees in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon wuzi in the tenth month of Yuanchu 1 (114), an eclipse occurred at ten degrees in Wei.

sentences.zh: 尾为后宫。

translations.literal: Wei is the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: Wei is the asterism of the imperial harem.

sentences.zh: 继嗣之宫也。

translations.literal: It is the palace of succession.
translations.idiomatic: It is the lodge that governs heirs and succession.

sentences.zh: 是时上甚幸阎贵人，将立，故示不善，将为继嗣祸也。

translations.literal: At this time the sovereign greatly favored Honored Person Yan and was about to establish her; therefore it showed not good—there would be calamity for succession.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor doted on Lady Yan and meant to make her empress; the eclipse foretold ill for the heir and the dynasty's line.

sentences.zh: 明年四月，遂立为后。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the next year, she was then established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: The following fourth month she was enthroned as empress.

sentences.zh: 后遂与江京、耿宝等共谗太子，废之。

translations.literal: Afterward she together with Jiang Jing, Geng Bao and others jointly slandered the heir apparent and deposed him.
translations.idiomatic: She then joined Jiang Jing, Geng Bao, and others in poisoning the heir apparent's name until he was cast aside.

sentences.zh: 二年九月壬午晦，日有蚀之，在心四度。

translations.literal: On the last day renwu of the ninth month of the second year, there was a solar eclipse, at four degrees in Xin.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on renwu in the ninth month of Yuanchu 2 (115), the sun was eclipsed at four degrees in the Heart mansion.

sentences.zh: 心为王者，明久失位也。

translations.literal: Xin is for the king; the brightness long lost its position.
translations.idiomatic: The Heart is the ruler's star; the eclipse meant the true king had long forfeited his seat.

sentences.zh: 三年三月二日辛亥，日有蚀之，在娄五度。

translations.literal: On the second day of the third month xinhai of the third year, there was a solar eclipse, at five degrees in Lou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, the second day of the third month of Yuanchu 3 (116), an eclipse fell at five degrees in Lou.

sentences.zh: 史官不见，辽东以闻。

translations.literal: The clerks of history did not see it; Liaodong reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Court astronomers missed it; Liaodong relayed the sighting.

sentences.zh: 四年二月乙已朔，日有蚀之，在奎九度。

translations.literal: On the yisi new-moon day of the second month of the fourth year, there was a solar eclipse, at nine degrees in Kui.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon yisi in the second month of Yuanchu 4 (117), the sun was eclipsed at nine degrees in Kui.

sentences.zh: 史官不见，七郡以闻。

translations.literal: The clerks of history did not see it; seven commanderies reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Capital scribes failed to record it; seven commanderies sent separate reports.

sentences.zh: 奎主武库兵。

translations.literal: Kui governs armory weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Kui presages the imperial arsenal and its arms.

sentences.zh: 其月十八日壬戌，武库火，烧兵器也。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day of that month renxu, the armory caught fire—it burned weapons.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu the eighteenth of that month the Luoyang armory burned, consuming stacks of weapons.

sentences.zh: 五年八月丙申朔，日有蚀之，在翼十八度。

translations.literal: On the bingshen new-moon day of the eighth month of the fifth year, there was a solar eclipse, at eighteen degrees in Yi.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon bingshen in the eighth month of Yuanchu 5 (118), an eclipse reached eighteen degrees in Yi.

sentences.zh: 史官不见，张掖以闻。

translations.literal: The clerks of history did not see it; Zhangye reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Astronomers at court did not see it; Zhangye Commandery reported the eclipse.

sentences.zh: 六年十二月戊午朔，日有食之，几尽，地如昏状。

translations.literal: On the wuwu new-moon day of the twelfth month of the sixth year, there was a solar eclipse; it was almost total; the earth was like dusk.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon wuwu in the twelfth month of Yuanchu 6 (119), a nearly total eclipse darkened the land like twilight.

sentences.zh: 在须女十一度，女主恶之。

translations.literal: It was at eleven degrees in Girl; the chief woman detested it.
translations.idiomatic: It struck eleven degrees in the Girl asterism—an ill omen for the ruling empress.

sentences.zh: 后二岁三月，邓太后崩。

translations.literal: After two years, in the third month, Empress Dowager Deng died.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, in the third month, Empress Dowager Deng passed away.

sentences.zh: 永宁元年七月乙酉朔，日有蚀之，在张十五度。

translations.literal: On the yiyou new-moon day of the seventh month of the first year of Yongning, there was a solar eclipse, at fifteen degrees in Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon yiyou in the seventh month of Yongning 1 (120), the sun was eclipsed at fifteen degrees in Zhang.

sentences.zh: 史官不见，酒泉以闻。

translations.literal: The clerks of history did not see it; Jiuquan reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The capital observatory missed it; Jiuquan sent word.

sentences.zh: 延光三年九月庚申晦，日有食之，在氐十五度。

translations.literal: On the last day gengshen of the ninth month of the third year of Yanguang, there was a solar eclipse, at fifteen degrees in Di.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on gengshen in the ninth month of Yanguang 3 (124), an eclipse occurred at fifteen degrees in Di.

sentences.zh: 氐为宿宫。

translations.literal: Di is the lodging palace.
translations.idiomatic: Di is the lodge of the ruler's private apartments.

sentences.zh: 宫，中宫也。

translations.literal: Palace means the central palace.
translations.idiomatic: Here "palace" denotes the empress's domain at the center of the court.

sentences.zh: 时上听中常侍江京、樊丰及阿母王圣等谗言，废皇太子。

translations.literal: At the time the sovereign listened to the slanderous words of Regular Attendants Jiang Jing and Fan Feng and of his nurse Wang Sheng and others, and deposed the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor trusted Jiang Jing, Fan Feng, and his wet nurse Wang Sheng, believed their lies, and deposed the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 四年三月戊午朔，日有蚀之，在胃十二度。

translations.literal: On the wuwu new-moon day of the third month of the fourth year, there was a solar eclipse, at twelve degrees in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon wuwu in the third month of Yanguang 4 (125), the sun was eclipsed at twelve degrees in Wei.

sentences.zh: 陇西、酒泉、朔方各以状上，史官不觉。

translations.literal: Longxi, Jiuquan, and Shuofang each submitted situation reports upward; the clerks of history did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: Longxi, Jiuquan, and Shuofang all filed reports, yet the capital historians failed to note the eclipse.

sentences.zh: 顺帝永建二年七月甲戌朔，日有蚀之，在翼九度。

translations.literal: On the jiaxu new-moon day of the seventh month of the second year of Yongjian of Emperor Shun, there was a solar eclipse, at nine degrees in Yi.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon jiaxu in the seventh month of Yongjian 2 (127), an eclipse struck nine degrees in Yi.

sentences.zh: 阳嘉四年闰月丁亥朔，日有蚀之，在角五度。

translations.literal: On the dinghai new-moon day of the intercalary month of the fourth year of Yangjia, there was a solar eclipse, at five degrees in Horn.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon dinghai in the intercalary month of Yangjia 4 (135), the sun was eclipsed at five degrees in Horn.

sentences.zh: 史官不见，零陵以闻。

translations.literal: The clerks of history did not see it; Lingling reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Court scribes missed it; Lingling Commandery reported the event.

sentences.zh: 永和三年十二月戊戌朔，日有独之，在须女十一度。

translations.literal: On the wuxu new-moon day of the twelfth month of the third year of Yonghe, there was a solar eclipse, at eleven degrees in Girl.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon wuxu in the twelfth month of Yonghe 3 (138), an eclipse occurred at eleven degrees in the Girl asterism.

sentences.zh: 史官不见，会稽以闻。

translations.literal: The clerks of history did not see it; Kuaiji reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The observatory at Luoyang saw nothing; Kuaiji relayed the eclipse.

sentences.zh: 明年，中常侍张逵等谋谮皇后父梁商欲作乱，推考，逵等伏诛也。

translations.literal: The next year Regular Attendants Zhang Kui and others plotted to slander the empress's father Liang Shang, wishing to charge rebellion; under investigation, Kui and others were executed.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Zhang Kui and other eunuchs tried to frame Liang Shang for treason; the plot collapsed and they were executed.

sentences.zh: 五年五月己丑晦，日有蚀之，在东井三十三度。

translations.literal: On the last day jichou of the fifth month of the fifth year, there was a solar eclipse, at thirty-three degrees in Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on jichou in the fifth month of Yonghe 5 (140), the sun was eclipsed at thirty-three degrees in Eastern Well.

sentences.zh: 东井，三辅宿。

translations.literal: Eastern Well is the lodge of the Three Supports.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Well governs the capital region of the Three Supports.

sentences.zh: 又近舆鬼，舆鬼为宗庙。

translations.literal: It is also near Yugi; Yugi is the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: It borders Yugi, the asterism of the imperial shrines.

sentences.zh: 其秋，西羌为寇，至三辅陵园。

translations.literal: That autumn the Western Qiang became raiders and reached the imperial tombs of the Three Supports.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Qiang raiders from the west broke through to the mausoleum parks around Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 六年九月辛亥晦，日有蚀之，在尾十一度。

translations.literal: On the last day xinhai of the ninth month of the sixth year, there was a solar eclipse, at eleven degrees in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on xinhai in the ninth month of Yonghe 6 (141), an eclipse fell at eleven degrees in Wei.

sentences.zh: 尾主后宫，继嗣之宫也。

translations.literal: Wei governs the rear palace; it is the palace of succession.
translations.idiomatic: Wei rules the harem and the matter of heirs.

sentences.zh: 以为继嗣不兴之象。

translations.literal: It was taken as an image of succession not rising.
translations.idiomatic: Readers took it as a sign that the imperial line would not flourish.

sentences.zh: 桓帝建和元年正月辛亥朔，日有蚀之，在营室三度。

translations.literal: On the xinhai new-moon day of the first month of the first year of Jianhe of Emperor Huan, there was a solar eclipse, at three degrees in Encampment.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon xinhai in the first month of Jianhe 1 (147), the sun was eclipsed at three degrees in Encampment.

sentences.zh: 史官不见，郡国以闻。

translations.literal: The clerks of history did not see it; commanderies and kingdoms reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Capital historians missed it; reports arrived from the provinces.

sentences.zh: 是时梁太后摄政。

translations.literal: At this time Empress Dowager Liang held the regency.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Liang was then regent for the boy emperor.

sentences.zh: 三年四月丁卯晦，日有蚀之，在东井二十三度。

translations.literal: On the last day dingmao of the fourth month of the third year, there was a solar eclipse, at twenty-three degrees in Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on dingmao in the fourth month of Jianhe 3 (149), an eclipse reached twenty-three degrees in Eastern Well.

sentences.zh: 例在永元十五年。

translations.literal: The precedent is in Yongyuan fifteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: The parallel case is discussed under Yongyuan 15.

sentences.zh: 东井主法，梁太后又听兄冀枉杀公卿，犯天法也。

translations.literal: Eastern Well governs law; Empress Dowager Liang again listened as her brother Ji wrongly killed dukes and ministers, offending Heaven's law.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Well stands for justice; the dowager let her brother Liang Ji murder ministers without cause—a breach of Heaven's law.

sentences.zh: 明年，太后崩。

translations.literal: The next year the empress dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the empress dowager died.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二年七月二日庚辰，日有蚀之，在翼四度。

translations.literal: On the second day of the seventh month gengchen of the second year of Yuanjia, there was a solar eclipse, at four degrees in Yi.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, the second day of the seventh month of Yuanjia 2 (152), the sun was eclipsed at four degrees in Yi.

sentences.zh: 史官不见，广陵以闻。

translations.literal: The clerks of history did not see it; Guangling reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang's astronomers saw nothing; Guangling reported the eclipse.

sentences.zh: 翼主倡乐。

translations.literal: Yi governs performers and music.
translations.idiomatic: Yi presides over music, dance, and court entertainments.

sentences.zh: 时上好乐过。

translations.literal: At the time the sovereign loved music excessively.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then addicted to spectacle and song.

sentences.zh: 永兴二年九月丁卯朔，日有蚀之，在角五度。

translations.literal: On the dingmao new-moon day of the ninth month of the second year of Yongxing, there was a solar eclipse, at five degrees in Horn.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon dingmao in the ninth month of Yongxing 2 (154), an eclipse occurred at five degrees in Horn.

sentences.zh: 角，郑宿也。

translations.literal: Horn is the lodge of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Horn corresponds to the old state of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 十一月，泰山盗贼群起，劫杀长吏。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month bandits on Mount Tai rose in groups, plundering and killing senior clerks.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month bandit gangs erupted on Mount Tai, robbing and murdering officials.

sentences.zh: 泰山于天文属郑。

translations.literal: Mount Tai in astronomical terms belongs to Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: By celestial mapping Mount Tai lies in the Zheng sector.

sentences.zh: 永寿三年闰月庚辰晦，日有蚀之，在七星二度。

translations.literal: On the last day gengchen of the intercalary month of the third year of Yongshou, there was a solar eclipse, at two degrees in the Seven Stars.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on gengchen in the intercalary month of Yongshou 3 (157), the sun was eclipsed at two degrees in the Seven Stars.

sentences.zh: 史官不见，郡国以闻，例在永元四年。

translations.literal: The clerks of history did not see it; commanderies and kingdoms reported it; the precedent is in Yongyuan fourth year.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial reports replaced a silent capital record; the parallel is under Yongyuan 4.

sentences.zh: 后二岁，梁皇后崩，翼兄弟被诛。

translations.literal: After two years Empress Liang died, and the Yi brothers were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Empress Liang died and her brothers in the Liang clan were put to death.

sentences.zh: 延熹元年五月甲戌晦，日有蚀之，在柳七度，京都宿也。

translations.literal: On the last day jiaxu of the fifth month of the first year of Yanxi, there was a solar eclipse, at seven degrees in Liu, the capital's lodging.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on jiaxu in the fifth month of Yanxi 1 (158), an eclipse struck Liu at seven degrees—the capital's own lodge.

sentences.zh: 八年正月丙甲晦，日有蚀之，在营室十三度。

translations.literal: On the last day bingjia of the first month of the eighth year of Yanxi, there was a solar eclipse, at thirteen degrees in Encampment.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on bingjia in the first month of Yanxi 8 (165), the sun was eclipsed at thirteen degrees in Encampment.

sentences.zh: 营室之中，女主象也。

translations.literal: Within Encampment is the image of the chief consort.
translations.idiomatic: Encampment is the mansion of the empress.

sentences.zh: 其二月癸亥，邓皇后坐酗，上送暴室，令自杀，家属被诛。

translations.literal: On its second month guihai, Empress Deng sat guilty of intoxication; the sovereign sent her to the Sudden Heat chamber, ordered her to commit suicide, and her family members were executed.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai in the second month Empress Deng was convicted of drunkenness, confined to the Sudden Heat ward, forced to kill herself, and her kin were executed.

sentences.zh: 吕太后崩时亦然。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Lü died it was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The same conjunction had appeared when Empress Dowager Lü died.

sentences.zh: 九年正月辛卯朔，日有蚀之，在营室三度。

translations.literal: On the xinmao new-moon day of the first month of the ninth year, there was a solar eclipse, at three degrees in Encampment.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon xinmao in the first month of Yanxi 9 (166), an eclipse fell at three degrees in Encampment.

sentences.zh: 史官不见，郡国以闻。

translations.literal: The clerks of history did not see it; commanderies and kingdoms reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Again the capital missed it; the regions reported the eclipse.

sentences.zh: 谷永以为三朝尊者恶之。

translations.literal: Gu Yong held that the venerable ones of the three courts detested it.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yong warned that the eclipse was ominous for the senior ministers of the three courts.

sentences.zh: 其明年，宫车晏驾。

translations.literal: The next year the palace carriage delayed its departure.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Emperor Huan died.

sentences.zh: 永康元年五月壬子晦，日有蚀之，在舆鬼一度。

translations.literal: On the last day renzi of the fifth month of the first year of Yongkang, there was a solar eclipse, at one degree in Yugi.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on renzi in the fifth month of Yongkang 1 (167), the sun was eclipsed at one degree in Yugi.

sentences.zh: 儒说壬子淳水日，而阳不克，将有水害。

translations.literal: Confucian explanation: renzi is a Chunshui day, and yang did not overcome; there will be water harm.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars call renzi a "Chunshui" day on which yang falters—foretelling catastrophic floods.

sentences.zh: 其八月，六州大水，勃海海溢。

translations.literal: That eighth month six provinces had great flood; the Bohai sea overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: That August six provinces were inundated and the Bohai tide surged over the coast.

sentences.zh: 灵帝建宁元年五月丁未朔，日有蚀之。

translations.literal: On the dingwei new-moon day of the fifth month of the first year of Jianning of Emperor Ling, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon dingwei in the fifth month of Jianning 1 (168), a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 冬十月甲辰晦，日有蚀之。

translations.literal: On the last day jiachen of the tenth month in winter, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on jiachen in the tenth month of that year, another eclipse darkened the sun.

sentences.zh: 二年十月戊戌晦，日有蚀之。

translations.literal: On the last day wuxu of the tenth month of the second year, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on wuxu in the tenth month of Jianning 2 (169), the sun was eclipsed again.

sentences.zh: 右扶风以闻。

translations.literal: Right Fufeng reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Youfufeng Commandery relayed the sighting.

sentences.zh: 三年三月丙寅晦，日有蚀之。

translations.literal: On the last day bingyin of the third month of the third year, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on bingyin in the third month of Jianning 3 (170), an eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 梁相以闻。

translations.literal: The chancellor of Liang reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor of Liang state reported it.

sentences.zh: 四年三月辛酉朔，日有蚀之。

translations.literal: On the xinyou new-moon day of the third month of the fourth year, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon xinyou in the third month of Jianning 4 (171), the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 熹平二年十二月癸酉晦，日有蚀之，在虚二度。

translations.literal: On the last day guiyou of the twelfth month of the second year of Xiping, there was a solar eclipse, at two degrees in Xu.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on guiyou in the twelfth month of Xiping 2 (173), an eclipse struck two degrees in Xu.

sentences.zh: 是时中常侍曹节、王甫等专权。

translations.literal: At this time Regular Attendants Cao Jie, Wang Fu and others monopolized power.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs Cao Jie and Wang Fu then dominated the government.

sentences.zh: 六年十月癸丑朔，日有蚀之。

translations.literal: On the guichou new-moon day of the tenth month of the sixth year, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon guichou in the tenth month of Xiping 6 (177), a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 赵相以闻。

translations.literal: The chancellor of Zhao reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor of Zhao Commandery reported it.

sentences.zh: 中平三年五月壬辰晦，日有蚀之。

translations.literal: On the last day renchen of the fifth month of the third year of Zhongping, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on renchen in the fifth month of Zhongping 3 (186), the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 六年四月丙午朔，日有蚀之。

translations.literal: On the bingwu new-moon day of the fourth month of the sixth year, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon bingwu in the fourth month of Zhongping 6 (189), a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 其月浃辰，宫车晏驾。

translations.literal: That month, after a twelve-day span, the palace carriage delayed its departure.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve days into that same month Emperor Ling died.

sentences.zh: 献帝初平四年正月甲寅朔，日有蚀之，在营室四度。

translations.literal: On the jiayin new-moon day of the first month of the fourth year of Chuping of Emperor Xian, there was a solar eclipse, at four degrees in Encampment.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon jiayin in the first month of Chuping 4 (193), the sun was eclipsed at four degrees in Encampment.

sentences.zh: 是时，李傕、郭汜专政。

translations.literal: At this time Li Jue and Guo Si monopolized government.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue and Guo Si were then dictating policy at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 兴平元年六月乙巳晦，日有蚀之。

translations.literal: On the last day yisi of the sixth month of the first year of Xingping, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on yisi in the sixth month of Xingping 1 (194), an eclipse darkened the sun.

sentences.zh: 建安五年九月庚午朔，日有蚀之。

translations.literal: On the gengwu new-moon day of the ninth month of the fifth year of Jian'an, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon gengwu in the ninth month of Jian'an 5 (200), the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 六年二月丁卯朔，日有蚀之。

translations.literal: On the dingmao new-moon day of the second month of the sixth year, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon dingmao in the second month of Jian'an 6 (201), another eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 十三年十月癸未朔，日有蚀之，在尾十二度。

translations.literal: On the guiwei new-moon day of the tenth month of the thirteenth year, there was a solar eclipse, at twelve degrees in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon guiwei in the tenth month of Jian'an 13 (208), the sun was eclipsed at twelve degrees in Wei.

sentences.zh: 十五年二月乙巳朔，日有蚀之。

translations.literal: On the yisi new-moon day of the second month of the fifteenth year, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon yisi in the second month of Jian'an 15 (210), a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 十七年六月庚寅晦，日有蚀之。

translations.literal: On the last day gengyin of the sixth month of the seventeenth year, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on gengyin in the sixth month of Jian'an 17 (212), the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 二十一年五月己亥朔，日有蚀之。

translations.literal: On the jihai new-moon day of the fifth month of the twenty-first year, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon jihai in the fifth month of Jian'an 21 (216), a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 二十四年二月壬子晦，日有蚀之。

translations.literal: On the last day renzi of the second month of the twenty-fourth year, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: At month's end on renzi in the second month of Jian'an 24 (219), the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 凡汉中兴十二世，百九十六年，日蚀七十二：朔三十二，晦三十七，月二日三。

translations.literal: In all, from Han's restoration through twelve reigns, one hundred ninety-six years, solar eclipses were seventy-two: new moon thirty-two, last day thirty-seven, second day of month three.
translations.idiomatic: Across the restored Han line—twelve reigns and one hundred ninety-six years—seventy-two solar eclipses were recorded: thirty-two on new moons, thirty-seven at month's end, and three on the second day.

sentences.zh: 光武建武七年四月丙寅，日有晕抱，白虹贯晕，在毕八度。

translations.literal: On the bingyin day of the fourth month of the seventh year of Jianwu of Guangwu, the sun had a halo with embrace; a white rainbow pierced the halo; it was at eight degrees in Bi.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin in the fourth month of Jianwu 7 (31), the sun wore a double halo pierced by a white rainbow at eight degrees in Bi.

sentences.zh: 毕为边兵。

translations.literal: Bi is border troops.
translations.idiomatic: Bi again betokened frontier arms.

sentences.zh: 秋，隗嚣反，侵安定。

translations.literal: In autumn Wei Xiao rebelled and invaded Anding.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Wei Xiao rose and struck into Anding.

sentences.zh: 灵帝时，日数出东方，正赤如血，无光，高二丈余乃有景。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Ling, the sun repeatedly came out in the east, proper red like blood, without light; only when more than two zhang high did it have brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ling the sun often rose in the east the color of clotted blood, dim and nearly lightless until it climbed more than two zhang above the horizon.

sentences.zh: 且入西方，去地二丈，亦如之。

translations.literal: Moreover when it entered the west, two zhang from the ground, it was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: When it set in the west, some two zhang above the horizon, it showed the same blood-red dimness.

sentences.zh: 其占曰，事天不谨，则日月赤。

translations.literal: Its prognostication says: serving Heaven without care, then sun and moon are red.
translations.idiomatic: The omen texts read: careless service to Heaven turns sun and moon the color of blood.

sentences.zh: 是时，月出入去地二三丈，皆赤如血者数矣。

translations.literal: At this time, when the moon rose and set two or three zhang from the ground, all were red like blood—several times.
translations.idiomatic: The moon, too, when it hung two or three zhang above the horizon at rising or setting, often glowed the same lurid red.

sentences.zh: 光和四年二月己巳，黄气抱日，黄白珥在其表。

translations.literal: On the jisi day of the second month of the fourth year of Guanghe, yellow vapor embraced the sun; yellow-white ear-rings were on its outer side.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi in the second month of Guanghe 4 (181), yellowish vapor ringed the sun, with pale yellow prominences flaring from its disk.

sentences.zh: 中平四年三月丙申，黑气大如瓜，在日中。

translations.literal: On the bingshen day of the third month of the fourth year of Zhongping, black vapor as large as a melon was within the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen in the third month of Zhongping 4 (187), a melon-sized black spot appeared on the face of the sun.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，日色赤黄，中有黑气如飞鹊，数月乃销。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, the sun's color was red-yellow; within it was black vapor like a flying magpie; several months then it dissipated.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhongping 5 (188) the solar disk turned dull red-yellow with a black streak like a darting magpie; the blemish lingered for months before fading.

sentences.zh: 六年二月乙未，白虹贯日。

translations.literal: On the yiwei day of the second month of the sixth year, a white rainbow pierced the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei in the second month of Zhongping 6 (189), a white rainbow spanned the sun.

sentences.zh: 献帝初平元年二月壬辰，白虹贯日。

translations.literal: On the renchen day of the second month of the first year of Chuping of Emperor Xian, a white rainbow pierced the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen in the second month of Chuping 1 (190), another white rainbow crossed the solar disk.

sentences.zh: 桓帝永寿三年十二月壬戌，月蚀非其月。

translations.literal: On the renxu day of the twelfth month of the third year of Yongshou of Emperor Huan, a lunar eclipse not in its proper month.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu in the twelfth month of Yongshou 3 (157), a lunar eclipse occurred out of season.

sentences.zh: 延熹八年正月辛巳，月蚀非其月。

translations.literal: On the xinsi day of the first month of the eighth year of Yanxi, a lunar eclipse not in its proper month.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi in the first month of Yanxi 8 (165), the moon was eclipsed at an improper time.

sentences.zh: 赞曰：皇极惟建，五事克端。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: the sovereign norm is only established; the five affairs are able to be correct.
translations.idiomatic: The summation reads: when the sovereign holds the center, the five royal duties align true.

sentences.zh: 罚咎入沴，逆乱浸干。

translations.literal: Punishment and blame enter calamity; rebellion and disorder soak and encroach.
translations.idiomatic: Punishments and faults curdle into cosmic disruption; rebellion seeps upward until it stains the throne.

sentences.zh: 火下水腾，木弱金酸。

translations.literal: Fire below, water rises; wood weak, metal sour.
translations.idiomatic: Fire sinks beneath mounting water; wood withers and metal turns brittle—each element out of true.

sentences.zh: 妖岂或妄，气炎以观。

translations.literal: Prodigies—how could they be perhaps false? By vapor flame observe.
translations.idiomatic: These portents are no idle tales: read them in the fevered breath of the age.
